analysis: The code first calls Integer.parseInt(ipPart, 16) which may throw NumberFormatException if ipPart is null, empty, or contains invalid hexadecimal characters, or if the parsed value exceeds int range. This exception will propagate out of the method. Next, it calls ipPart.charAt(0) which could throw IndexOutOfBoundsException if ipPart is an empty string. However, for an empty string, Integer.parseInt already throws NumberFormatException, so charAt(0) is never reached. Similarly, for null input, Integer.parseInt throws NumberFormatException. Therefore, the only runtime exceptions that can be thrown are NumberFormatException (both from parseInt and the explicit throw), which is an expected part of the method's contract. No additional runtime exception handling is needed within this snippet.
